Proximates: non-starch polysaccharide, the Englyst method. This row used to read "englyst fibre (g)", which is what the method is called but not what the column is called. CoFID carries both fibre conventions and they are not interchangeable: NSP excludes resistant starch and lignin and so runs below an AOAC figure for the same food. NSP is kept because it is the convention this table already chose and because CoFID populates it for 2433 of 2889 foods against 1473 for AOAC -- but note that USDA, CIQUAL and AFCD all report AOAC-style total dietary fibre, so fibre is the one canonical key whose denominator differs by source

Vitamins: this column is retinol equivalents (RE), not retinol activity equivalents (RAE) -- they are different quantities that can differ by up to 2x for carotene-rich foods (RE historically used a 1:6 beta-carotene:retinol ratio; RAE uses 1:12). The aggregate RE figure alone cannot be converted to RAE without the underlying carotene breakdown, which this column does not carry, so it is dropped rather than stored under vitamin_a_rae. The canonical vocabulary has no separate RE key; retinol and carotene_beta are mapped individually below instead
